description:
FILED s507c (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-05) from #2690's -c probes; PRE-EXISTING on main ac2fec1e (and on the plain run, not only -c).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
  perl -e 'use List::Util; print 0+$!, "\n"; die "x\n"'; echo $?    -> x / 2 / rc=2
  pcl  -e 'use List::Util; print 0+$!, "\n"; die "x\n"'; echo $?    -> x / 0 / rc=255
  perl -e 'use strict; print 0+$!, "\n"; die "x\n"'                 -> 0 / rc=255   (strict.pm is found in the FIRST @INC dir)
  and under -c: printf 'use List::Util qw(sum);\nBEGIN { die "begin died\n" }\n' > c7.pl; perl -c c7.pl -> rc 2, pcl -c c7.pl -> rc 255.

CAUSE (read, the cheap measurement is the third line above): perl's `require` walks @INC and every directory that does not hold the file leaves ENOENT in errno; a later `die` exits with $! when it is nonzero.  PCL's module search (p-find-module-in-inc) probes with probe-file, which never touches PCL's *p-stored-errno*, so $! stays 0 and an uncaught die exits 255.
An exit status a shell script or a test harness reads: an everyday program that `use`s a module from a later @INC directory and then dies exits 2 under perl and 255 under PCL.
FIX DIRECTION: the search records ENOENT in $! (the %p-io-errno-fail 2 the failure path already uses) when it had to skip at least one directory -- measure which @INC position perl's own modules sit in (List::Util is in the arch dir, strict in lib/) and probe `$!` after `use` for three modules at three positions.
subject: A die after a `use` of a module found past the first @INC directory exits 2 under perl ($! is the ENOENT the @INC search left) and 255 under PCL ($! stays 0) -- `perl -e 'use List::Util; die "x\n"'` rc 2, pcl rc 255; also `pcl -c` on a dying BEGIN (PRE-EXISTING, found by s507c)
